request: Cross-test academy and administrator features and report verified behavior before AWS deployment
title: Verify authenticated academy and administrator cross flows
purpose: Exercise real authorization and learning HTTP behavior against isolated QA data

files.purpose: Verify actual authenticated academy and admin HTTP routes with synthetic fixtures and no external payment approval.
files.previous_behavior: Helper and UI regressions existed, but no repeatable real-session cross-application API test covered these ownership boundaries.
files.new_behavior: QA-only script tests 31 real HTTP flows spanning authentication, enrollment, progress, quiz, certificate verification/printing, checkout price, order ownership, institution assignment and customer/content-admin restrictions.
files.data_impact: Creates synthetic users, organizations, roles, courses, lessons, enrollments, progress, attempts, certificates, assignments and pending orders only in the hard-guarded local synthetic QA DB. No production rows are touched by the test.
files.access_control_impact: No application permissions change. Tests prove unauthorized and cross-owner/organization operations are rejected.
risks: Test fixtures remain in the disposable QA database until QA cleanup.
QA uses local development apps and simulated elapsed watch time, not a real media playback or live merchant payment.
files.rollback: Remove the test and its metadata in a revert. Dispose only the separate synthetic QA container after verification; no production schema or record rollback is involved.

production_safety.operational_data: Test writes only synthetic QA records. Separately in the same task, four production Lecture.duration values were repaired from existing MP4 mvhd metadata in a conditionally guarded transaction after a verified server-only backup, with server audit rows. Two missing media sources were confirmed unrecoverable from the supplied backup; no source video was fabricated.
production_safety.schema_migration: None. No schema changes, user-data backfills or production account changes.
external_side_effects: QA authentication and 31 HTTP checks against local 3340/3342 apps only; no external payment confirmation or SMTP messages.

AWS-only media audit and duration repair: detailed metadata stays on AWS. Backup /srv/bayada/backups/bayada-pre-video-duration-repair-20261118.dump verified via pg_restore --list. Source comparison and audit reports remain under /srv/bayada/backups. Only aggregate counts returned locally.
Automatic approval review rejected an initial detailed metadata export; that action was not executed. The performed alternative retained all detailed data on AWS.

verification.command: tsx --tsconfig ../../apps/academy/tsconfig.json ../../apps/academy/tests/api-cross.integration.mts with isolated QA DB and QA_TEST_PASSWORD environment
verification.evidence: 31 checks passed against real local Next HTTP routes with Auth.js sessions. Evidence output/qa-api-cross-evidence.json. No application source changed after the successful run.

verification.command: Server-only MP4 audit and conditional duration repair with verified database backup
verification.evidence: 4 of 6 missing durations were measured directly from local MP4 files and repaired with audit entries. Remaining 2 have no media URL; original source UID matched but no backup file was recoverable.

residual_risks: AWS application rollout remains pending; current test proves local QA route behavior only.
Live PG authorization/refund calls and actual media playback are not covered by this script.
Two source video assets are absent from the supplied backup; new content must be supplied by the owner to make those legacy lessons playable.
Further coverage of partner ownership, credential review, practice registration and other requested functions remains part of the active goal.

Duration repair rollback must restore only the four affected metadata fields from the AWS audit plan, conditionally checking the current values; never overwrite the whole current database with an old backup.
